evidence.claim: In 1950, Skousen, Isbell & Johnston Contracting Company won the contract for the canyon project, the first four-lane divided stretch of U.S. Route 66 built in New Mexico.
evidence.quote: In 1950, the Tijeras Canyon job was the largest road project ever let in the State of New Mexico. It also carried the honor of being the first U. S. Route 66 four-lane divided highway built in New Mexico. Skousen, Isbell & Johnston Contracting Company was awarded the contract.

evidence.claim: Work finished in 1951; Interstate 40 now traverses the canyon along historic Route 66.

evidence.quote: Tijeras is at the junction of Tijeras Canyon, leading to the west, toward Albuquerque, and Cedro Canyon, leading to the south, toward the Manzano Mountains.

evidence.claim: Ancestral Puebloans occupied the Tijeras Pueblo site from about 1313 CE to 1425 CE.
evidence.quote: The site was occupied by Ancestral Puebloans from about 1313 CE to 1425 CE.

evidence.claim: Its first phase had about 200 rooms in terraced buildings forming a U, with a large ceremonial kiva at the center.
evidence.quote: In the first phase of its occupation the Tijeras Pueblo had about 200 rooms in terraced buildings arranged in a "U" shape with a large ceremonial Kiva at the center.

evidence.claim: Partial abandonment after about 1360 gave way to rebuilding about 1390, but the pueblo never regained its earlier size.
evidence.quote: The pueblo was partially abandoned after about 1360 but rebuilding began about 1390, although the pueblo never regained its previous size.
